name: Sonnet macro/sector rotation
strategy: Catalyst-driven sector rotation with a reduced financials/regional-bank overweight after the hike thesis weakened, plus defensive/healthcare longs, a consumer-discretionary short and ~46% cash.
reassessment_note: Sept payrolls came in at 29K vs 84K expected, unemployment 4.2%, and October hike odds collapsed to ~16-21% from 36-64%. Financials lagged on the day and my XLF/KRE overweight was built on a hawkish-hike thesis, so I halve conviction there (XLF 17->10, KRE 19->10) while keeping exposure because a December hike is still priced as likely and 10y yields are ~5.25%. Other legs unchanged; freed weight goes to cash at 4%.

positions.thesis: Biotech benefits from lower hike odds and soft data; small 6% size unchanged, wide stop.
Defensive healthcare ballast against a slowing labor market; size unchanged.
Financials lagged on the weak jobs day and hike-driven thesis is damaged; trimmed to 10% but retained since December hike remains priced and soft landing would help.
Regional banks gain from higher-for-longer curve but face credit/NIM worries on weak jobs; cut to 10% from 19%.
Low-vol hedge for growth scare; unchanged small size.
Consumer discretionary exposed to 5%+ long yields and a 29K payroll print; cyclicals led the 10-02 rally so size kept at 9% with a 12% stop.
